data.diagnosis: Cellular angiofibroma of the lower female genital tract
data.description: A rare benign mesenchymal tumor, usually arising in the vulvovaginal or paravaginal region. It is typically small, well circumscribed, composed of bland spindle cells, collagenous stroma, and numerous hyalinized vessels.
symptoms_in_common: Small, well-circumscribed pelvic/perivaginal soft-tissue mass on MRI and ultrasound
Predominantly low-to-intermediate T2 signal compatible with fibrous/collagenous tissue
Whorled or heterogeneous internal appearance
Grossly well-defined pale tan-white lesion
Histology showing bland spindle-cell proliferation with prominent vessels and collagenized stroma

data.description: A benign spindle-cell neoplasm that can occur along the embryonic milk line, including the vulvovaginal and inguinal regions. It is usually circumscribed and contains myofibroblasts, abundant hyalinized collagen, and variable thin-walled vessels.
symptoms_in_common: Well-demarcated small soft-tissue mass
Low T2 signal areas consistent with abundant fibrous collagen
Gross pale, firm, lobulated mass
Bland spindle-cell histology
Prominent collagen deposition highlighted by trichrome-type staining
symptoms_not_in_common: Numerous conspicuous hyalinized vessels are more characteristic of cellular angiofibroma than classic mammary-type myofibroblastoma

data.description: A benign mesenchymal tumor of the vulva or vagina, generally small and circumscribed. Histologically it contains stromal spindle or epithelioid cells concentrated around numerous blood vessels.
symptoms_in_common: Small, well-circumscribed vulvovaginal/perivaginal mass
Benign-appearing localized lesion on imaging
Spindle-cell lesion with a prominent vascular component
symptoms_not_in_common: The marked collagenized or hyalinized stroma is less typical
Classic alternating hypercellular and hypocellular perivascular zones are not clearly demonstrated
Low T2 signal due to dense fibrous tissue is less typical than in collagen-rich tumors

data.description: A locally infiltrative mesenchymal tumor usually occurring in the pelvis, perineum, or vulvovaginal region of women. It is characterized by myxoid stroma and numerous vessels and may recur after excision.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic or perivaginal soft-tissue mass
Vascular stromal lesion on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears small and sharply circumscribed rather than infiltrative
The imaging appearance is relatively low T2 signal rather than markedly T2-hyperintense myxoid signal
Histology appears collagenized/fibrous rather than predominantly hypocellular myxoid stroma
No large translevator or deep pelvic extension is shown

data.description: A benign smooth-muscle tumor that may arise from the uterus, cervix, or rarely the vagina. Leiomyomas are commonly well circumscribed and often demonstrate low T2 signal because of smooth muscle and fibrous tissue.
symptoms_in_common: Well-defined pelvic mass
Low T2 signal compatible with smooth muscle or fibrous tissue
Whorled internal imaging appearance
Gross firm pale tan-white tissue
Spindle-cell morphology
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent small vessels with hyalinized vascular walls favor cellular angiofibroma over an ordinary leiomyoma
Histology appears more collagenous and vascular than typical intersecting smooth-muscle fascicles
The lesion's apparent lower genital tract/perivaginal location is less typical than uterine origin

data.diagnosis: Acute pyelonephritis (focal or multifocal bacterial nephritis)
data.description: Bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma that can produce focal wedge-shaped areas of edema, altered echogenicity, reduced perfusion, and heterogeneous signal on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Focal heterogeneous renal parenchymal abnormality on ultrasound
Patchy or wedge-shaped renal signal abnormality on MRI
Areas of relatively decreased or altered intrarenal Doppler perfusion
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, flank pain, dysuria, urinary frequency, pyuria, or laboratory evidence of infection was provided

data.diagnosis: Acute focal bacterial nephritis (acute lobar nephronia)
data.description: A localized severe form of renal infection, intermediate between uncomplicated pyelonephritis and renal abscess, causing a poorly defined focal inflammatory renal mass without a drainable fluid collection.
symptoms_in_common: Ill-defined focal renal lesion rather than a sharply circumscribed mass
Heterogeneous renal cortical/medullary appearance
Abnormal focal perfusion pattern on color Doppler
Focal signal changes in the kidney on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No systemic infectious symptoms or elevated inflammatory markers were provided
No definite central liquefaction or drainable abscess cavity is shown

data.description: Ischemic necrosis of renal tissue caused by interruption of arterial blood supply, typically producing peripheral wedge-shaped lesions with reduced or absent perfusion.
symptoms_in_common: Wedge-like peripheral renal parenchymal abnormalities
Focal perfusion abnormality on Doppler imaging
Focal MRI signal changes that may follow a vascular territory
symptoms_not_in_common: No sudden severe flank pain was provided
No history of embolic disease, atrial fibrillation, vascular procedure, hypercoagulability, hematuria, or elevated lactate dehydrogenase was provided

data.description: A localized collection of pus within the kidney, often developing as a complication of pyelonephritis or hematogenous infection; imaging may show a focal heterogeneous lesion with peripheral vascularity.
symptoms_in_common: Focal renal parenchymal lesion
Heterogeneous appearance on ultrasound and MRI
Possible surrounding inflammatory changes and altered vascularity
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly defined fluid cavity, internal debris, or rim-enhancing collection is provided
No fever, sepsis, persistent urinary infection, or flank tenderness was provided

data.diagnosis: Renal neoplasm, such as renal cell carcinoma
data.description: A primary renal tumor that may appear as a focal heterogeneous renal mass with internal vascularity and variable MRI signal characteristics.
symptoms_in_common: Focal renal lesion on ultrasound
Heterogeneous lesion appearance on MRI
Detectable intralesional or adjacent vascularity on Doppler imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: The described wedge-shaped or inflammatory-appearing pattern is less typical of a discrete renal tumor
No hematuria, weight loss, palpable mass, or metastatic findings were provided

data.diagnosis: Hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus
data.description: Primary liver cancer arising from hepatocytes, often presenting as a large heterogeneous hepatic mass and capable of invading the portal venous system.
symptoms_in_common: Large heterogeneous mass centered in the left hepatic lobe
Apparent invasion or thrombus within a portal venous branch near the mass
Distortion of normal liver architecture
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, liver disease history, or laboratory values are provided

data.description: A primary malignancy of intrahepatic bile ducts that can appear as a large infiltrative hepatic mass, sometimes with vascular encasement or invasion.
symptoms_in_common: Large infiltrative-appearing hepatic mass
Heterogeneous enhancement/attenuation of the lesion
Possible adjacent portal venous involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No biliary duct dilatation is clearly demonstrated
No jaundice, pruritus, weight loss, or cholestatic laboratory abnormalities are provided

data.description: Secondary malignant deposits in the liver from an extrahepatic primary cancer; metastases may be solitary or multifocal and can become large and necrotic.
symptoms_in_common: Large heterogeneous liver lesion
Possible central necrosis or variable internal attenuation
Mass effect on adjacent hepatic and upper abdominal structures
symptoms_not_in_common: No known extrahepatic primary malignancy is provided
Portal vein tumor thrombus is more characteristic of hepatocellular carcinoma than most metastatic tumors
No additional hepatic lesions are clearly visible on this single image

data.description: A mitochondrial inherited optic neuropathy causing sequential or bilateral central visual loss, optic-disc vascular changes in early stages, and later optic atrophy with retinal nerve fiber layer loss.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral optic disc pallor/optic atrophy
Marked bilateral retinal nerve fiber layer thinning on OCT
Prominent/tortuous peripapillary retinal vessels
No obvious compressive intracranial lesion on the displayed MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No acute or subacute central visual loss is described
No color-vision loss is described
No central scotoma is described
No family history or mitochondrial inheritance pattern is provided

data.diagnosis: Autosomal dominant optic atrophy (DOA, commonly OPA1-related)
data.description: An inherited optic neuropathy characterized by slowly progressive bilateral optic atrophy, usually with temporal disc pallor, reduced color vision, central visual-field defects, and diffuse or temporal retinal nerve fiber layer thinning.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral optic disc pallor/optic atrophy
Bilateral reduction in average retinal nerve fiber layer thickness
Superior and inferior retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
Absence of an obvious brain or spinal cord structural cause on the displayed MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No slowly progressive visual impairment is described
No dyschromatopsia is described
No central or centrocecal visual-field defect is described
No family history of optic atrophy is provided

data.diagnosis: Chronic bilateral optic neuritis or demyelinating optic neuropathy
data.description: Inflammatory or demyelinating injury to the optic nerves can result in optic disc pallor and persistent retinal nerve fiber layer thinning after one or more episodes of optic neuritis; causes include multiple sclerosis, MOG-antibody disease, and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
symptoms_in_common: Optic disc pallor compatible with prior optic nerve injury
Bilateral retinal nerve fiber layer thinning on OCT
Brain and spinal MRI are relevant investigations for an inflammatory/demyelinating optic neuropathy
symptoms_not_in_common: No painful visual loss is described
No acute optic neuritis episodes are described
No optic nerve enhancement or demyelinating brain/spinal lesions are evident in the provided images
No neurologic symptoms such as myelitis, weakness, numbness, or bladder dysfunction are described

data.description: A chronic progressive optic neuropathy, usually associated with elevated or susceptible intraocular pressure, producing retinal nerve fiber layer loss and characteristic optic-disc cupping with visual-field defects.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
Superior and inferior sectoral abnormalities on OCT
symptoms_not_in_common: The fundus appearance is more suggestive of optic pallor than classic glaucomatous cupping
No elevated intraocular pressure is reported
No glaucomatous visual-field loss is described
Prominent retinal vessel tortuosity is not a typical primary feature of glaucoma

data.diagnosis: Acquired hepatocerebral degeneration due to chronic liver disease
data.description: A neurologic syndrome associated with chronic liver failure or portosystemic shunting, often causing manganese deposition in the basal ganglia and resulting in characteristic T1 MRI hyperintensity with movement and cognitive symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: T1 hyperintensity in the basal ganglia compatible with metal deposition
Bilateral basal ganglia abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Homozygous pathogenic ATP7B c.2333G>T (p.Arg778Leu) variant
Corneal Kayser-Fleischer-ring-like findings
Basal ganglia T2, FLAIR, and diffusion abnormalities suggesting degenerative injury rather than isolated manganese deposition

data.description: A toxic movement-disorder syndrome caused by chronic manganese exposure or impaired biliary manganese excretion; it commonly affects the globus pallidus and produces T1 hyperintensity on brain MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Deep basal ganglia T1 hyperintensity suggesting metal deposition
Bilateral basal ganglia involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Homozygous pathogenic ATP7B c.2333G>T (p.Arg778Leu) variant
Corneal Kayser-Fleischer-ring-like findings
T2, FLAIR, and diffusion-weighted basal ganglia changes indicating degeneration
No reported occupational, environmental, or parenteral-nutrition manganese exposure

data.description: Inflammation and fluid accumulation in the bursa over the tip of the elbow (olecranon), often caused by pressure, repetitive trauma, or injury.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent localized swelling over the posterior elbow/olecranon
Redness over the swollen area
Appearance consistent with a superficial fluid-filled bursal enlargement
symptoms_not_in_common: Bruise-like purple discoloration is less typical unless there has been trauma or bleeding into the bursa

data.description: Infection of the olecranon bursa, commonly caused by bacteria entering through a skin break, abrasion, or puncture near the elbow.
symptoms_in_common: Marked swelling directly over the olecranon
Overlying redness and inflammatory skin changes
Possible focal darker red area that could reflect skin irritation or infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, drainage, open wound, or systemic illness is provided
No reported severe pain or tenderness

data.description: A bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissues that causes expanding redness, warmth, swelling, and tenderness.
symptoms_in_common: Redness involving the posterior elbow region
Soft-tissue swelling
Inflammatory-appearing skin discoloration
symptoms_not_in_common: A sharply localized, rounded swelling centered over the olecranon is more suggestive of bursitis than uncomplicated cellulitis
No reported fever, chills, skin break, or diffuse spreading erythema

data.diagnosis: Traumatic olecranon bursitis or elbow contusion
data.description: Swelling and bruising after direct impact or repetitive pressure on the elbow, which may cause bleeding or fluid accumulation in the olecranon bursa.
symptoms_in_common: Swelling over the point of the elbow
Purple-red bruising/discoloration
Localized inflammatory changes
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of a fall, direct blow, repetitive pressure, or other trauma is provided
Diffuse redness may be more prominent than expected for a simple contusion

data.description: Enlargement of nasopharyngeal lymphoid tissue (adenoids), which can narrow the nasopharyngeal airway and contribute to upper-airway obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging appearance of prominent soft tissue in the nasopharynx
Narrowing of the nasopharyngeal airway
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, such as nasal obstruction, snoring, mouth breathing, recurrent otitis media, or sleep apnea, were provided

data.diagnosis: Obstructive sleep apnea due to upper-airway soft-tissue crowding
data.description: Sleep-related recurrent upper-airway obstruction that may be associated with enlarged adenoids, tonsils, tongue base, or other pharyngeal soft tissues.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging suggestion of upper-airway narrowing at the nasopharyngeal/oropharyngeal level
Prominent pharyngeal soft tissues
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported snoring
No witnessed apneas
No daytime sleepiness
No nocturnal choking or restless sleep history

data.description: Inflammation or infection in the retropharyngeal space that can cause prevertebral soft-tissue thickening and potentially compromise the airway; an abscess generally shows a drainable fluid collection, often with rim enhancement on contrast imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Possible increased prevertebral/retropharyngeal soft tissue on the sagittal neck image
Potential upper-airway narrowing
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported
No sore throat reported
No neck pain or neck stiffness reported
No dysphagia or odynophagia reported
No reported rim-enhancing fluid collection or gas-containing abscess on the provided image

data.description: Hypoglycemia caused by insulin secretagogue medications, which stimulate pancreatic insulin release and therefore produce high insulin and high C-peptide levels.
symptoms_in_common: Marked hypoglycemia (glucose 2.4 mmol/L)
Elevated insulin level
Elevated C-peptide level
Low beta-hydroxybutyrate consistent with insulin-mediated hypoglycemia
symptoms_not_in_common: No sulfonylurea or meglitinide exposure is documented

data.description: Diffuse pancreatic beta-cell hyperfunction causing excessive endogenous insulin secretion, often resulting in recurrent hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia.
symptoms_in_common: Hypoglycemia
Elevated endogenous insulin
Elevated C-peptide
Suppressed ketone production during hypoglycemia
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of recurrent postprandial hypoglycemia is documented
No history of bariatric or upper gastrointestinal surgery is documented

data.description: A rare cause of spontaneous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia caused by insulin autoantibodies that bind and later release insulin.
symptoms_in_common: Hypoglycemia
Markedly elevated insulin level
C-peptide is present, supporting endogenous insulin secretion rather than injected insulin
symptoms_not_in_common: Insulin concentrations in insulin autoimmune syndrome are often extremely high relative to the reported value
No insulin autoantibody result is provided
No exposure to associated medications or supplements, such as alpha-lipoic acid or sulfhydryl-containing drugs, is documented

data.description: A congenital chest-wall anomaly in which adjacent ribs are partially or completely joined by bone or cartilage. It may be isolated or associated with vertebral segmentation abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Ultrasound appearance of abnormal continuity/crowding between the 7th, 8th, and 9th ribs
Altered rib contour in the imaged lower thoracic chest wall
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, pain, trauma history, respiratory symptoms, or systemic findings were provided

data.description: A developmental rib anomaly in which a rib divides into two branches, most often anteriorly. It is usually asymptomatic and may be found incidentally on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Possible irregular or branching contour of the imaged 8th rib
Abnormal relationship of the 8th rib to adjacent 7th and 9th ribs
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpable chest-wall prominence was reported
No pain or respiratory symptoms were provided
The images may suggest fusion rather than the typical separated branches of a bifid rib

data.diagnosis: Healed rib fracture with callus formation
data.description: Prior rib trauma can heal with irregular bony callus, cortical thickening, deformity, or bridging between adjacent ribs. Imaging correlation with radiographs or CT is generally needed.
symptoms_in_common: Irregular contour and apparent thickening of the 8th rib
Possible abnormal bridging or close apposition involving adjacent ribs
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of chest trauma was provided
No focal chest-wall pain or tenderness was reported
No acute fracture features or surrounding soft-tissue hematoma were described

data.description: A benign or secondary condition characterized by multiple gas-filled cysts within the submucosa or subserosa of the intestinal wall, often involving the colon. Endoscopy may show smooth, cystic, polyp-like submucosal lesions, and histology can show empty cystic spaces with foreign-body giant cell reaction.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple clustered, grape-like intramural gas lucencies in the colonic wall on contrast radiography
Smooth, rounded, submucosal cystic lesions seen during colonoscopy
Endoscopic appearance of translucent polypoid elevations with intact mucosa
Intramural empty spaces/cysts on histology
Foreign-body type multinucleated giant cell reaction around cystic spaces on histology

data.description: A rare benign lymphatic malformation that can produce multiple submucosal cystic lesions in the colon. Lesions contain lymphatic fluid rather than gas and may resemble cystic polyps endoscopically.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple smooth submucosal polypoid or cyst-like colonic lesions on colonoscopy
Potentially benign-appearing intact mucosa over lesions
Cystic spaces within the bowel wall may be present histologically
symptoms_not_in_common: Clustered intramural gas lucencies on radiography are not typical
Gas-filled rather than fluid-filled cyst appearance is not typical
Foreign-body giant cell reaction around empty gas cysts is not typical

data.diagnosis: Colonic lipomatosis or multiple colonic lipomas
data.description: Benign fatty tumors or diffuse fatty infiltration of the colonic submucosa that can create smooth, rounded submucosal bulges during colonoscopy.
symptoms_in_common: Smooth, rounded submucosal colonic protrusions on endoscopy
Generally intact overlying colonic mucosa
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple grape-like intramural gas collections on contrast radiography are not typical
Translucent gas-cyst appearance is not typical
Histologic empty cystic spaces with giant-cell reaction are not typical
Lipomas would show mature adipose tissue rather than intramural gas cysts

data.description: La bioquímica de la sangre periférica mostró leucocitos de 7.700/μL con eosinofilia marcada (53,5%), anemia (glóbulos rojos 366 ×10^4/μL, Hgb 8,6 g/dL) y CRP elevada (2,66 mg/dL). Las plaquetas fueron de 25,5 ×10^4/μL. ANA, anticuerpo Jo-1, RF, PR-ANCA, MPO-ANCA y marcadores infecciosos para VHB, VHC y VIH fueron negativos. Las pruebas de función renal y hepática estuvieron dentro de los límites normales. La gasometría arterial mostró pH 7,549 con pCO2 bajo (27,1 mmHg) y pO2 68,2 mmHg.

data.diagnosis: Leucemia eosinofílica crónica, no especificada de otra manera (CEL-NOS)
data.description: Una neoplasia mieloide clonal caracterizada por hipereosinofilia persistente, maduración anormal de eosinófilos, citopenias y/o hematopoyeesis displásica, a menudo con anomalías citogenéticas tras la exclusión de neoplasias eosinofílicas definidas por reordenamiento específico.
symptoms_in_common: Eosinofilia periférica en sangre marcada (53,5%; recuento absoluto de eosinófilos aproximadamente 4.100/μL)
Anemia (hemoglobina 8,6 g/dL)
Froto periférico anormal con precursores eosinofílicos y características displásicas
Células similares a megaloblastos y neutrófilos hipersegmentados irregulares en el frotis
Anomalía citogenética que afecta a los cromosomas 1 y 7
PCR elevada
No se proporcionó evidencia de hepatitis autoinmune, asociada al ANCA, vírica o eosinofilia secundaria relacionada con el VIH
symptoms_not_in_common: Recuento total de leucocitos normal a pesar de una eosinofilia marcada
No se documentan esplenomegalia, síntomas constitucionales ni afectación cardíaca, neurológica, gastrointestinal o cutánea mediada por eosinófilos

data.description: Una neoplasia mieloide solapada en la que la producción ineficaz y displásica de células sanguíneas coexiste con características proliferativas como la eosinofilia; pueden estar presentes anomalías cromosómicas y células displásicas.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia
Eosinofilia marcada
Displasia de la sangre periférica, incluyendo neutrófilos hipersegmentados irregulares
Formas eosinófilas inmaduras que incluyen mielocitos eosinofílicos, metamieloicitos y bandas
Anomalía citogenética que afecta a los cromosomas 1 y 7
El recuento de plaquetas no se reduce gravemente, lo que puede ocurrir en neoplasias solapadas
symptoms_not_in_common: No se ha reportado monocitosis persistente
No se ha reportado trombocitosis ni leucocitosis
No se ha reportado esplenomegalia
No se proporcionan hallazgos de médula ósea para determinar el grado de displasia, fibrosis o porcentaje de blastos

data.diagnosis: Neoplasia mieloide/linfoide con eosinofilia y reorganización del gen tirosina quinasa
data.description: Un grupo de neoplasias hematológicas clonales impulsadas por reordenamientos que involucran genes como PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1 o PCM1-JAK2. Comúnmente causan eosinofilia marcada y pueden producir anemia y maduración mieloide anormal.
symptoms_in_common: Eosinofilia marcada
Anemia
Formas inmaduras de granulocitos eosinofílicos en la sangre periférica
Posible anomalía citogenética clonal
Las pruebas autoinmunes y víricas infecciosas comunes negativas apoyan la consideración de un trastorno clonal eosinofílico primario
symptoms_not_in_common: No se documenta ningún reordenamiento específico de PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, PCM1-JAK2 u otra reorganización de quinasas
No se ha reportado esplenomegalia
No se han reportado hepatomegalia, linfadenopatía ni infiltración de órganos relacionada con eosinófilos
El recuento total normal de leucocitos es menos típico que la leucocitosis que se observa a menudo en estos trastornos

data.description: Un diagnóstico de exclusión definido por hipereosinofilia persistente, generalmente con daño orgánico asociado a eosinófilos, tras excluir causas secundarias y clonales.
symptoms_in_common: Hipereosinofilia con un recuento absoluto de eosinófilos superior a 1.500/μL
ANA negativo, factor reumatoide, pruebas ANCA y marcadores infecciosos virales probados
La hipoxemia leve puede reflejar potencialmente afectación eosinofílica pulmonar
symptoms_not_in_common: La anemia y los hallazgos prominentes de la disolución de sangre prefieren un trastorno de la médula clonal en lugar de un HES idiopático
La anomalía citogenética que involucra los cromosomas 1 y 7 no es típica del HES idiopático
No hay daño documentado en órganos mediados por eosinófilos
No se han reportado erupciones cutáneas, asma, neuropatía, miocardiopatía, síntomas gastrointestinales ni manifestaciones tromboembólicas

data.description: A clonal histiocytic neoplasm characterized by proliferation of Langerhans cells, often showing grooved nuclei and immunoreactivity for CD1a, langerin/CD207, and S100. It can involve lymph nodes, bone, skin, lungs, liver, spleen, kidneys, and the gastrointestinal or genitourinary tract.
symptoms_in_common: Multifocal abdominal and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy on CT/PET imaging
Possible renal or perirenal involvement
Soft-tissue or genitourinary tract involvement suggested by ultrasound
Histology showing a histiocytic cellular infiltrate with characteristic irregular/grooved nuclei
Immunohistochemical pattern consistent with Langerhans-cell markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked stool burden/constipation on abdominal radiograph is nonspecific and not a classic primary manifestation
No characteristic lytic bone lesions are shown
No typical skin rash, diabetes insipidus, or pulmonary cystic disease is described

data.description: A non-Langerhans histiocytic disorder causing painless lymph-node enlargement and sometimes extranodal disease involving the skin, upper respiratory tract, kidneys, or retroperitoneum. Histology typically shows large S100-positive histiocytes with emperipolesis.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent multifocal lymphadenopathy
Possible extranodal abdominal, renal, retroperitoneal, or genitourinary involvement
Histiocyte-rich tissue appearance on pathology
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent immunophenotype suggesting CD1a/langerin-positive cells would be atypical because Rosai-Dorfman disease is usually CD1a negative
Classic emperipolesis is not clearly demonstrated in the provided pathology images
Constipation/stool retention is nonspecific and not a typical defining feature

data.description: Lymphoma is a malignant proliferation of lymphoid cells that can present with widespread lymphadenopathy and extranodal abdominal involvement, including renal, retroperitoneal, bowel, and pelvic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the chest, abdomen, and retroperitoneum
Possible renal involvement
Abdominal soft-tissue abnormalities
PET-avid nodal disease would be compatible with lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: The pathology appears histiocytic rather than a monomorphic lymphoid neoplasm
Immunostaining suggestive of Langerhans-cell differentiation would not be typical for lymphoma
No described constitutional symptoms such as fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss

data.description: A rare non-Langerhans histiocytic neoplasm, usually driven by MAPK-pathway mutations, that can involve retroperitoneal tissue, kidneys, cardiovascular structures, bones, and the central nervous system. Histology generally shows foamy CD68-positive, CD1a-negative histiocytes.
symptoms_in_common: Possible retroperitoneal and renal/perirenal involvement
Multisystem infiltrative disease pattern
Histiocytic infiltrate on pathology
symptoms_not_in_common: This condition is uncommon in children
Diffuse lymphadenopathy is less typical than in Langerhans cell histiocytosis or lymphoma
CD1a-positive or langerin-positive staining would argue against Erdheim-Chester disease
Typical symmetric osteosclerosis of the long bones is not shown

diagnoses.name: Mixed-cellularity subtype of classic Hodgkin's lymphoma
diagnoses.title: Mixed cellularity classical Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: La evaluación inicial mostró leucocitosis con neutrofilia, linfopenia severa, trombocitopenia marcada, hiponatremia y hipocloremia leves, creatinina elevada, magnesio bajo, AST/ALT elevados, hiperbilirrubinemia y haptoglobina baja. La hemoglobina y el hematócrito estaban ligeramente elevados; el fibrinógeno y el pH venoso estaban normales.

Una malaria potencialmente mortal causada por Plasmodium falciparum, caracterizada por alta parásitemia, hemólisis, trombocitopenia y posible disfunción renal y hepática. Las imágenes de la citología muestran formas intraeritrocíticas del anillo compatibles con la malaria, y el patrón de prueba rápida es compatible con la infección por P. falciparum.
symptoms_in_common: Trombocitopenia marcada
Haptoglobina baja que indica hemólisis
Hiperbilirrubinemia
AST y ALT elevados
Creatinina elevada que sugiere lesión renal aguda
Linfopenia grave
Froto sanguíneo periférico con parásitos intraeritrocíticos en forma de anillo

Coagulopatía compatible con CID
Lesiones cutáneas púrpúricas/equimóticas
Elevación de lactato y acidosis metabólica
Lesión renal aguda
Elevación de enzimas hepáticas durante el shock
Anomalías leucocitarias, incluyendo posible leucopenia precoz y leucocitosis posterior
symptoms_not_in_common: La imagen del frotis proporcionada parece mostrar bastones alargados en lugar de los diplococos gram-negativos típicos de Neisseria meningitidis
No se reportaron fiebre, dolor de cabeza, rigidez en el cuello, alteración del estado mental ni meningitis
No se proporcionó ningún pródromo respiratorio ni exposición conocida a contacto cercano

data.description: Una infección grave causada por una bacteria marina gram-negativa curvada, generalmente tras la ingestión de mariscos crudos o la exposición al agua de mar, especialmente en pacientes con enfermedad hepática crónica. Puede causar shock séptico, CID, lesiones cutáneas bullosas o púrpuras y fallo multiorgánico.
symptoms_in_common: Fisiología severa de sepsis con lactato elevado y acidosis metabólica
Trombocitopenia progresiva y coagulopatía
Lesiones cutáneas púrpúricas/equimóticas
Lesión renal aguda
AST/ALT elevado
leucocitosis con desplazamiento a la izquierda tras un recuento inicial bajo de glóbulos blancos
En el frotis se pueden observar organismos curvados o en forma de bastón Gramnegativos
symptoms_not_in_common: No se proporcionó exposición al agua de mar, heridas marinas, mariscos ni mariscos crudos
No se proporcionó enfermedad hepática crónica, cirrosis ni sobrecarga de hierro
No se reportaron bullas hemorrágicas características ni celulitis dolorosa explícita

data.description: Infección invasiva grave por Streptococcus pneumoniae, especialmente en pacientes asplénicos o inmunodeprimidos, que puede causar shock séptico, CIV, púrpura fulminana, lesión renal aguda y disfunción hepática.
symptoms_in_common: Anomalías leucocitarias asociadas a la sepsis
Trombocitopenia y anemia progresivas
Coagulopatía que empeora es compatible con la CID
Lesiones púrpricas/equimóticas compatibles con púrpura fulminans
Elevación de lactato y acidosis metabólica
Lesión renal aguda
Enzimas hepáticas elevadas
symptoms_not_in_common: La imagen del frotis no muestra los diplococos típicos de forma de lanceta gram-positivos de Streptococcus pneumoniae
No se reportaron síntomas de neumonía, meningitis, otitis, sinusitis ni esplenectomía
La radiografía torácica no demuestra claramente una consolidación neumónica lobar focal

data.diagnosis: Left atrial myxoma with cardioembolic acute ischemic stroke
data.description: A left atrial myxoma is a benign primary cardiac tumor that can release tumor fragments or thrombus, causing systemic arterial emboli including acute cerebral infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Acute diffusion-restricted infarct involving the left cerebral hemisphere, compatible with acute ischemic stroke
Intracranial arterial occlusion or markedly reduced flow on MR angiography
Intracardiac mass seen on echocardiography, compatible with an atrial myxoma
Imaging pattern consistent with an embolic source from the heart
symptoms_not_in_common: No constitutional symptoms such as fever, weight loss, fatigue, or elevated inflammatory markers are provided
No reported positional dyspnea, syncope, or symptoms of mitral-valve obstruction

data.diagnosis: Cardioembolic left middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke
data.description: An acute ischemic stroke occurs when an embolus blocks a cerebral artery. Cardiac emboli may arise from atrial tumors, atrial thrombus, atrial fibrillation, valvular disease, or other intracardiac sources.
symptoms_in_common: Large acute cortical and subcortical diffusion-restricted lesion in the left cerebral hemisphere
MR angiographic evidence of proximal intracranial arterial occlusion or severe flow reduction
Cardiac mass on echocardiography that could serve as an embolic source
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical neurologic deficits, such as aphasia, facial weakness, right-sided weakness, or sensory loss, are described
No reported atrial fibrillation or other arrhythmia

data.diagnosis: Left atrial thrombus with cerebral embolization
data.description: A thrombus within the left atrium or left atrial appendage can embolize into the systemic circulation and obstruct a cerebral artery, producing an acute ischemic infarct.
symptoms_in_common: Echocardiographic intracardiac mass that could represent thrombus
Acute ischemic infarction in an arterial cerebral territory
Intracranial arterial occlusion compatible with embolization
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported atrial fibrillation, severe mitral stenosis, markedly reduced left ventricular function, or other common thrombus-promoting cardiac condition
The apparent pedunculated intracardiac mass may be more suggestive of myxoma than thrombus

diagnoses.name: MELAS syndrome
diagnoses.title: MELAS - [Mitochondrial encephalopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes] syndrome

data.description: Laboratory data on admission showed elevated liver tests and bilirubin: ALT 327 U/L, AST 104 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 172 U/L, total bilirubin 5.8 mg/dL, and CA 19-9 73 U/mL. Lipase was mildly elevated at 72 U/L. White blood cell count, hemoglobin, platelets, electrolytes, renal function, and albumin were within normal limits. On admission at the second hospital, bilirubin remained elevated at 6.7 mg/dL, AST increased to 267 U/L, ALT decreased to 85 U/L, alkaline phosphatase was 150 U/L, glucose 124 mg/dL, and CA 19-9 was 79 U/mL.
A malignant epithelial tumor of the pancreatic ducts, commonly arising in the pancreatic head and causing obstruction of the distal common bile duct, jaundice, and elevated CA 19-9.
symptoms_in_common: Marked hyperbilirubinemia consistent with obstructive jaundice
Elevated alkaline phosphatase
Elevated AST and ALT
Elevated CA 19-9
Mild lipase elevation
Imaging appearance of biliary obstruction and a pancreatic/peripancreatic mass
Histology compatible with infiltrating adenocarcinoma with desmoplastic stromal reaction
Possible liver metastatic lesions on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal albumin despite apparent advanced malignant disease
Normal blood counts
No reported weight loss
No reported abdominal or back pain
No reported new-onset diabetes or marked hyperglycemia

data.description: A bile-duct adenocarcinoma arising in the distal common bile duct. It often presents with painless obstructive jaundice and can be difficult to distinguish from pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive bilirubin elevation
Cholestatic liver-test abnormalities with elevated alkaline phosphatase
Elevated AST and ALT due to biliary obstruction
Mild CA 19-9 elevation
Biliary duct obstruction on imaging
Adenocarcinoma on cytology or biopsy
Possible hepatic metastatic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild lipase elevation is less characteristic unless there is secondary pancreatic involvement
No reported pruritus
No reported pale stools or dark urine
No reported fever or cholangitis
Normal white blood cell count

data.description: A malignant tumor arising from the ampulla of Vater, where the bile duct and pancreatic duct enter the duodenum. It commonly causes early biliary obstruction and jaundice.
symptoms_in_common: Obstructive hyperbilirubinemia
Elevated alkaline phosphatase and transaminases
Mild elevation of CA 19-9
Mild lipase elevation from partial pancreatic duct obstruction
Distal biliary obstruction on imaging
Adenocarcinoma histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Possible extensive liver lesions would be more suggestive of advanced disease rather than a typical early ampullary presentation
No reported gastrointestinal bleeding or anemia
Normal hemoglobin
No reported abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting

data.description: Gallbladder adenocarcinoma is a biliary tract malignancy that may invade the hepatic hilum or extrahepatic bile ducts, causing jaundice and cholestatic liver-test abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated bilirubin
Elevated alkaline phosphatase and liver enzymes
Elevated CA 19-9
Adenocarcinoma morphology can overlap with pancreaticobiliary tumors
Possible liver involvement or metastases
symptoms_not_in_common: Imaging centered on the pancreatic/distal bile-duct region would be less typical than a gallbladder mass
Mild lipase elevation is not typical
No reported right-upper-quadrant pain
No reported gallbladder wall mass or gallstones
Normal white blood cell count without inflammatory findings

data.description: A rare mechanical twisting of the gallbladder around its cystic duct and vascular pedicle, which can obstruct blood flow and cause acute ischemic cholecystitis.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging appearance suggesting abnormal gallbladder positioning
Possible twisted or tapered cystic duct/pedicle appearance near the gallbladder neck
Possible separation of the gallbladder from the liver bed
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as sudden right-upper-quadrant pain, nausea, vomiting, fever, or palpable abdominal mass were provided
No definite imaging evidence of a markedly distended, ischemic, or necrotic gallbladder is provided

data.description: Inflammation of the gallbladder, most commonly caused by obstruction of the cystic duct by a gallstone.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormality localized to the gallbladder/cystic duct region on imaging
Possible gallbladder wall or pericholecystic inflammatory change
symptoms_not_in_common: No right-upper-quadrant abdominal pain was reported
No fever, nausea, vomiting, leukocytosis, or positive Murphy sign was reported
No definite gallstone, substantial gallbladder distension, or prominent pericholecystic fluid is described

data.description: Blockage of the cystic duct by a gallstone, which may cause biliary colic or progress to acute cholecystitis.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging finding centered at the gallbladder neck or cystic duct region
Possible focal narrowing or obstruction near the gallbladder outlet
symptoms_not_in_common: No gallstones are definitively visible or described
No episodic postprandial right-upper-quadrant pain was reported
No jaundice, nausea, vomiting, fever, or laboratory evidence of biliary obstruction was provided

data.diagnosis: Juvenile osteochondritis dissecans of the medial femoral condyle
data.description: A focal osteochondral disorder in which subchondral bone and overlying cartilage of the femoral condyle become damaged; it commonly affects adolescents and often involves the lateral aspect of the medial femoral condyle.
symptoms_in_common: Left knee radiographs suggest a focal subchondral irregularity or lucent osteochondral lesion at the femoral condyle
Knee joint alignment is otherwise relatively preserved
No obvious acute displaced fracture is seen
symptoms_not_in_common: No knee pain, swelling, locking, catching, or activity-related symptoms were provided
No loose osteochondral body is clearly demonstrated on the supplied radiographs

data.diagnosis: Normal developmental irregularity of the distal femoral epiphysis
data.description: Children and adolescents can have benign irregular ossification of the femoral condyles that can mimic an osteochondral lesion, particularly when there is no associated clinical knee dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Subtle femoral condylar contour or subchondral irregularity on radiographs
No obvious aggressive bone destruction
No acute fracture or dislocation is visible
symptoms_not_in_common: Patient age and skeletal maturity were not provided
No information is available regarding absence of pain or normal physical examination findings

data.diagnosis: Osteochondral injury or healing osteochondral fracture of the femoral condyle
data.description: An osteochondral injury involves trauma to articular cartilage and adjacent subchondral bone; radiographs may show focal irregularity, flattening, or a lucent defect in the involved condyle.
symptoms_in_common: Possible focal osteochondral/subchondral irregularity at the femoral condyle
No gross knee dislocation is present
No major displaced fracture is identified
symptoms_not_in_common: No trauma history was provided
No acute joint effusion, severe swelling, inability to bear weight, or mechanical symptoms were provided
No clearly displaced osteochondral fragment is visible

data.description: A lymphocyte-mediated inflammatory disorder of hair follicles that can cause perifollicular scaling, follicular keratotic papules, and permanent scarring alopecia.
symptoms_in_common: Scalp hair loss with areas suggestive of cicatricial alopecia
Perifollicular scaling and follicular keratotic papules
Follicular plugging on clinical and dermoscopic images
Perifollicular inflammatory infiltrate and fibrosis on histology
Reduced or absent follicular openings in affected scalp areas

data.description: A rare variant of lichen planopilaris characterized by scarring scalp alopecia together with widespread follicular keratotic papules; loss of axillary or pubic hair may also occur.
symptoms_in_common: Scarring-appearing alopecia of the scalp
Numerous disseminated follicular keratotic papules on the trunk and extremities
Perifollicular scale and follicular plugging
Lichenoid perifollicular inflammation on histologic images
symptoms_not_in_common: Axillary or pubic hair loss is not described

data.diagnosis: Discoid lupus erythematosus of the scalp
data.description: A chronic cutaneous lupus subtype that commonly produces inflammatory plaques with follicular plugging, pigment change, and irreversible scarring alopecia.
symptoms_in_common: Scalp alopecia with possible scarring
Follicular plugging
Perifollicular inflammatory changes
Pigmented follicular lesions on dermoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Well-demarcated erythematous scaly plaques are not clearly shown
Widespread keratosis-pilaris-like follicular papules are less typical

data.description: A follicular form of lichen planus in which keratotic papules develop around hair follicles and may coexist with lichen planopilaris of the scalp.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple small follicular keratotic papules over the trunk and limbs
Perifollicular pigmentation and scale
Scalp follicular involvement with hair loss
Lymphocytic inflammation centered around hair follicles on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Typical violaceous polygonal flat-topped lichen planus papules are not described
Oral or genital mucosal lesions are not described

data.description: A thrombotic occlusive disease of small dermal blood vessels that causes recurrent, painful ulcers around the ankles and feet and may heal with white stellate scars (atrophie blanche). Histology commonly shows hyalinized, thickened superficial dermal vessels with fibrin thrombi and relatively limited inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Ulcerated lesion centered around the ankle
Purpuric-brown discoloration surrounding the ulcer
Small recurrent-appearing lesions near the ankle
Healing with crusting and residual hyperpigmentation/scarring
Histologic appearance of small-vessel occlusion/hyalinization
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear white stellate atrophie blanche scars are visible
Pain severity is not provided
No recurrent course or thrombophilia history is provided

data.description: A skin-limited necrotizing vasculitis involving small- and medium-sized arteries in the deep dermis or subcutaneous tissue. It can produce tender nodules, livedo reticularis, purpura, and painful ulcers on the lower legs and ankles.
symptoms_in_common: Lower-leg and ankle ulceration
Purpuric or violaceous discoloration around lesions
Possible multiple lesions at different healing stages
Vascular injury visible on skin histology
symptoms_not_in_common: No tender subcutaneous nodules are described
No livedo reticularis is clearly shown
No systemic features such as fever, arthralgia, neuropathy, renal disease, or abdominal pain are provided
The histology shown does not clearly demonstrate classic necrotizing arteritis with prominent inflammatory infiltration

data.description: A painful ischemic ulcer due to hypertensive arteriolosclerosis of small cutaneous vessels, classically affecting the lateral lower leg, supramalleolar region, or Achilles-area skin in patients with longstanding hypertension and often diabetes.
symptoms_in_common: Ulcer in the supramalleolar/lateral ankle region
Dark violaceous or necrotic-appearing surrounding skin
Histologic suggestion of small-vessel wall thickening/arteriolosclerosis
Ulcer healing with scar and pigmentary change
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypertension history is not provided
Diabetes history is not provided
Severe disproportionate pain, a typical feature, is not reported
The lesion location is not definitively lateral supramalleolar in every image

data.description: A severe ischemic skin disorder caused by calcification and thrombosis of small dermal and subcutaneous vessels, most often in advanced chronic kidney disease or dialysis patients. It produces exquisitely painful violaceous plaques that progress to necrotic ulcers.
symptoms_in_common: Violaceous-brown skin discoloration surrounding an ulcer
Necrotic and ulcerative skin lesion
Vascular occlusive changes could be considered on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: No kidney failure, dialysis, calcium-phosphate abnormality, or warfarin exposure is provided
No calcification of vessel walls is clearly demonstrated in the shown histology
The lesions appear relatively localized to the ankle rather than widespread
Severe pain is not reported

data.diagnosis: Chronic venous leg ulcer with stasis dermatitis
data.description: Venous insufficiency can cause edema, brown hemosiderin pigmentation, eczematous dermatitis, and chronic ulceration, usually in the gaiter area around the medial ankle.
symptoms_in_common: Ankle-region ulceration
Brown-red hyperpigmentation around the lesion
Chronic-appearing skin change and healing crusts
Lower-leg distribution
symptoms_not_in_common: No leg edema, varicosities, or venous insufficiency history is provided
The ulcer is not clearly in the typical medial malleolar location
The focal vascular histology may be more suggestive of an occlusive vasculopathy than uncomplicated venous stasis
No broad eczematous stasis dermatitis is described

data.description: A high-grade malignant vascular tumor composed of atypical epithelioid endothelial cells. Tumor cells may form poorly developed vascular channels and show intracytoplasmic vacuoles; endothelial immunostains such as CD31, ERG, FLI1, and CD34 are typically positive.
symptoms_in_common: Histology shows markedly atypical epithelioid cells with pleomorphism
Cells have cytoplasmic vacuolation suggestive of primitive vascular lumen formation
Immunohistochemical images show diffuse tumor-cell staining compatible with an endothelial phenotype
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical presentation, lesion location, bleeding, pain, or systemic symptoms are provided
No definite well-formed vascular channels are demonstrated in the supplied images

data.description: A malignant vascular neoplasm of intermediate biologic behavior, usually composed of epithelioid endothelial cells with cytoplasmic vacuoles in a myxohyaline or fibrous stroma. It generally expresses endothelial markers including CD31, ERG, FLI1, and CD34.
symptoms_in_common: Epithelioid tumor-cell morphology
Intracytoplasmic vacuoles that can represent primitive vascular spaces
Apparent diffuse immunohistochemical staining consistent with vascular differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: The marked cytologic atypia and high-grade appearance are less typical than in conventional epithelioid hemangioendothelioma
A characteristic myxohyaline stroma and cords of cells are not clearly evident
No organ site or multifocal disease pattern is provided

data.description: An aggressive soft-tissue sarcoma composed of large epithelioid and rhabdoid-appearing malignant cells. It often expresses cytokeratin, EMA, and sometimes CD34, with loss of INI1/SMARCB1 in most cases.
symptoms_in_common: Sheets of atypical epithelioid cells
Pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli
Possible rhabdoid or vacuolated cytoplasmic appearance
Diffuse immunohistochemical tumor-cell staining could fit epithelial-marker expression
symptoms_not_in_common: No information is provided regarding a deep proximal soft-tissue mass or anatomic location
Granuloma-like necrosis, a common feature in some epithelioid sarcomas, is not clearly shown
INI1/SMARCB1 loss and keratin/EMA staining results are not specified

diagnoses.title: Gastrointestinal stromal tumour of unspecified gastrointestinal sites

data.diagnosis: Gastric glomus tumor (large or potentially malignant gastric glomus tumor)
data.description: A rare mesenchymal tumor derived from modified smooth-muscle glomus cells, most often arising in the gastric antrum. It typically shows uniform round cells arranged around branching blood vessels and expresses smooth-muscle markers such as SMA, while CD34 may highlight the vascular network rather than tumor cells.
symptoms_in_common: Large well-defined heterogeneous upper-abdominal/gastric-region mass on CT
Grossly circumscribed yellow-tan to hemorrhagic tumor
Histology showing relatively uniform round-to-oval cells in sheets and perivascular arrangements
Prominent delicate vascular network within the tumor
Immunohistochemical appearance compatible with diffuse smooth-muscle-marker staining and vascular CD34 staining
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, laboratory findings, age, or sex were provided
The very large tumor size is less typical of conventional benign gastric glomus tumors

data.description: GIST is the most common mesenchymal neoplasm of the stomach, arising from interstitial cells of Cajal. It can form a large exophytic gastric mass with hemorrhage or necrosis and usually expresses KIT (CD117) and DOG1.
symptoms_in_common: Large exophytic upper-abdominal mass apparently related to the stomach
Heterogeneous appearance with possible hemorrhagic or necrotic areas
Bulky, well-circumscribed gross tumor
Mesenchymal-appearing tumor on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Uniform round perivascular cells are less typical than the spindle-cell or epithelioid morphology of most GISTs
Diffuse smooth-muscle-marker pattern with CD34 limited to vessels would favor glomus tumor over GIST
No reported KIT, DOG1, or tumor-cell CD34 positivity
No clinical symptoms, laboratory findings, age, or sex were provided

data.description: These are smooth-muscle tumors of the stomach. Leiomyoma is benign, whereas leiomyosarcoma is malignant and generally shows infiltrative growth, significant atypia, necrosis, and increased mitotic activity.
symptoms_in_common: Large gastric-region soft-tissue mass
Gross yellow-tan and hemorrhagic tumor areas can occur in malignant smooth-muscle tumors
Possible positivity for smooth-muscle immunohistochemical markers
Mesenchymal tumor morphology
symptoms_not_in_common: The illustrated cells appear more round and perivascular than elongated spindle smooth-muscle cells
No definite intersecting fascicles of spindle cells are shown
No described marked pleomorphism, atypical mitoses, or overt coagulative tumor necrosis required to strongly support leiomyosarcoma
No clinical symptoms, laboratory findings, age, or sex were provided

data.description: Gastric schwannoma is an uncommon benign peripheral-nerve-sheath tumor, usually composed of spindle cells with a peripheral lymphoid cuff and diffuse S-100/SOX10 positivity.
symptoms_in_common: Gastric-region mass on imaging
Circumscribed mesenchymal tumor
May be asymptomatic until large
symptoms_not_in_common: The histology does not primarily show spindle cells, nuclear palisading, or a peripheral lymphoid cuff
Perivascular round-cell architecture is not typical
The gross hemorrhagic/yellow appearance and very large size are less typical for gastric schwannoma
No reported diffuse S-100 or SOX10 positivity
No clinical symptoms, laboratory findings, age, or sex were provided

data.description: A mosaic keratinization disorder presenting as localized, linear or segmental hyperkeratotic verrucous plaques. Histology shows epidermolytic hyperkeratosis with vacuolization of suprabasal keratinocytes and prominent keratohyalin granules.
symptoms_in_common: Localized extensive hyperpigmented verrucous and hyperkeratotic plaque in the axillary/chest region
Multiple clustered papules with a cobblestoned surface
Segmental or unilateral distribution
Histology showing epidermolytic hyperkeratosis, coarse keratohyalin granules, and vacuolated keratinocytes
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly documented linear distribution following Blaschko lines
No reported congenital onset or childhood onset
No reported associated skeletal, neurologic, or ocular abnormalities

data.description: A benign hamartomatous proliferation of epidermis that usually presents as persistent hyperpigmented, rough, papillomatous, or verrucous plaques, often in a unilateral or linear pattern.
symptoms_in_common: Hyperpigmented thickened plaque
Verrucous papillomatous surface
Clustered keratotic papules
Localized unilateral involvement of the trunk/axilla
Chronic-appearing plaque morphology
symptoms_not_in_common: Epidermolytic changes on histology are a specific subtype rather than a feature of all verrucous epidermal nevi
No reported linear Blaschkoid pattern
No reported onset at birth or early childhood

data.description: A keratin 1 or keratin 10 disorder characterized by epidermolytic hyperkeratosis. In mosaic forms, disease may be restricted to a localized segment of skin rather than causing generalized ichthyosis.
symptoms_in_common: Marked hyperkeratosis
Verrucous thickened skin
Histologic epidermolytic hyperkeratosis with suprabasal keratinocyte vacuolization and coarse keratohyalin granules
Possible localized mosaic distribution
symptoms_not_in_common: No generalized scaling or diffuse ichthyosis is shown
No history of neonatal blistering is provided
No widespread flexural hyperkeratosis is described
Lesion is sharply localized rather than generalized

data.description: A malignant cartilage-producing tumor arising in soft tissues rather than directly from bone; it can form a large lobulated pelvic mass with chondroid calcification.
symptoms_in_common: Large left pelvic/iliac-fossa soft-tissue mass
Lobulated internal and peripheral calcifications with a chondroid appearance on CT
Heterogeneous signal and enhancement on MRI
Metabolically active lesion on PET imaging
No obvious destructive osseous origin on pelvic radiograph/CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, patient age, or duration of illness are provided
No definite adjacent bone invasion is shown

data.description: A rare aggressive subtype of extraskeletal chondrosarcoma composed of undifferentiated cells and cartilage, often presenting as a calcified soft-tissue mass.
symptoms_in_common: Large deep soft-tissue mass in the pelvis
Prominent stippled, ring-like, or arc-like calcified matrix
Heterogeneous MRI appearance
FDG-avid/metabolically active mass
Apparent soft-tissue origin without a clear primary bone lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: No evidence of metastatic disease is provided
No constitutional symptoms such as weight loss or fever are provided

data.description: A malignant soft-tissue sarcoma that may occur near joints or in deep pelvic soft tissues and can contain focal or extensive calcification.
symptoms_in_common: Deep pelvic soft-tissue mass
Heterogeneous enhancement on MRI
Calcifications within the mass
Increased metabolic activity on PET
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion does not have a clearly joint-centered origin
The extensive chondroid-type calcification is more suggestive of a cartilaginous tumor
No clinical history of pain, swelling, or limited movement is provided

data.description: A rare high-grade malignant soft-tissue tumor that produces osteoid or bone matrix outside the skeleton, usually appearing as a mineralized soft-tissue mass.
symptoms_in_common: Large soft-tissue mass
Marked mineralization/calcification on CT
Heterogeneous MRI appearance
PET avidity suggesting active tumor tissue
No definite continuity with adjacent pelvic bone
symptoms_not_in_common: The calcifications appear more lobulated/chondroid than densely cloud-like osteoid matrix
No bone formation pattern typical of osteosarcoma is clearly demonstrated
No clinical symptoms are supplied

data.description: A benign uterine smooth-muscle tumor that may undergo hyaline degeneration and dystrophic calcification, sometimes becoming a large pelvic mass.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic mass
Presence of calcification
Potential mass effect on adjacent pelvic structures
symptoms_not_in_common: Mass appears eccentric in the left iliac fossa rather than clearly uterine in origin
Calcification pattern is not the typical coarse whorled or popcorn-like leiomyoma pattern
Marked heterogeneous enhancement and PET avidity are less typical for a benign calcified leiomyoma
No uterine enlargement, abnormal bleeding, or gynecologic symptoms are provided

data.diagnosis: Síndrome de persona rígida clásico (SPS) asociado a anticuerpos anti-GAD
data.description: Trastorno neurológico autoinmune caracterizado por rigidez muscular progresiva, espasmos dolorosos e hiperexcitabilidad del sistema motor. Frecuentemente se asocia a anticuerpos contra la descarboxilasa del ácido glutámico (anti-GAD) y actividad muscular continua en EMG.
symptoms_in_common: Fenotipo documentado de síndrome de persona rígida clásico
Anticuerpos anti-GAD elevados (2000 U/ml)
Actividad continua de unidades motoras en EMG
Hiperexcitabilidad del reflejo de parpadeo
Discapacidad motora grave previa, con uso de silla de ruedas
Mejoría clínica con inmunoterapia previa (IVIG y plasmaféresis)

data.diagnosis: Encefalomielitis progresiva con rigidez y mioclonías (PERM)
data.description: Forma más grave del espectro de los trastornos de rigidez muscular autoinmunes. Puede producir rigidez, espasmos, mioclonías, hiperexcitabilidad del tronco encefálico y alteraciones autonómicas; suele asociarse a anticuerpos anti-glicina, aunque también puede haber anti-GAD.
symptoms_in_common: Rigidez e hiperexcitabilidad muscular compatibles con el espectro SPS
Actividad continua de unidades motoras en EMG
Hiperexcitabilidad del reflejo de parpadeo
Enfermedad de probable mecanismo autoinmune
Respuesta a inmunoterapia
symptoms_not_in_common: No se documentan mioclonías
No se documentan signos de encefalopatía o afectación cerebral
No se documentan disfunción autonómica, como fluctuaciones de presión arterial, taquicardia o sudoración intensa
No se documentan signos bulbares o respiratorios
El fenotipo está descrito específicamente como SPS clásico, no como PERM

data.description: Trastorno de hiperexcitabilidad de nervios periféricos que causa actividad muscular continua, fasciculaciones, calambres, rigidez, mioquimia y relajación muscular retrasada. Puede tener una base autoinmune y responder a inmunoterapia.
symptoms_in_common: Actividad muscular continua de unidades motoras en EMG
Rigidez o hiperactividad muscular

data.description: Emergency department presentation with severe hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia: serum calcium 5.4 mg/dL (ionized calcium 0.57 mmol/L) and phosphorus 10.6 mg/dL, with persistently low calcium 5.1 mg/dL and phosphorus 10.0 mg/dL at 1 hour. data.description: Los datos de laboratorio muestran citopenias progresivas y empeoramiento de la función hepática y renal durante el ingreso: leucopenia (leucocitos 3810/μL antes del ingreso, 5190 al ingreso, 3430 al día 5 hospitalario), anemia (hemoglobina 12,9 a 9,4 g/dL) y trombocitopenia (plaquetas 87.000 a 99.000/μL).
